sections.markdown:
## G — Sharing the road with vulnerable users and large vehicles
Completion index for Sharing the road with vulnerable users and large vehicles: the knowledge and continuation chunks contain the source-bound rules, conditions and distinctions. The accuracy chunk keeps unverified or dynamic claims as debt.
The exact missed-question allowance is sourced in A; percentage and time-limit values stay unknown. Demand and competitive research are unresolved in their respective chunks.

corpus_stability.reason: Corpus is the frozen July handbook snapshot; future issuer changes require a new source registration, rather than silent updates to this corpus.

verification_debt.claim_text: Demand evidence for Sharing the road with vulnerable users and large vehicles remains unresolved.
Competitor evidence for Sharing the road with vulnerable users and large vehicles remains unresolved.

The children-near-roadway instruction on physical page ninety-six continues onto ninety-seven with its unexpected-entry qualifier. Nearby complete child-safety instructions are covered; this complete cross-page instruction remains unresolved under the one-page fact binding.

The horse-passing instruction spans physical pages ninety-seven and ninety-eight. Approaching-rider slowing, no horn and control-difficulty response have local support, but the complete passing-room instruction needs a supported multi-page fact binding.

The bicycle straight-through red-light permission on physical page ninety-eight continues onto ninety-nine to complete the close-enough-to-be-a-hazard qualifier. That complete exception is withheld as coverage debt rather than truncating its yielding condition.

The repeated intersection-look discussion spans physical pages ninety-nine and one hundred. The local repeated-scan instruction is covered; the full closing rationale and numeric travel-distance example are not represented as a complete one-page fact.

The passing-distance paragraph starts on physical page one hundred and continues onto one hundred one with the pavement-edge distance and emergency-space explanation. The complete paragraph requires a multi-page binding; the independently complete motorist passing-clearance rules on one hundred one are covered.

The first sharrow-purpose bullet begins on physical page one hundred one and completes on one hundred two with parked-door collision avoidance. The complete multi-page bullet is coverage debt; other complete purposes are locally sourced.

Sharrow and Bicycles May Use Full Lane visual recognition, and any other sharing-road illustrations in the mapped pages, have not received semantic image review. Text meanings are covered; image-based practice must wait.

Physical page one hundred six states that all hazardous-material vehicles stop at all railroad crossings. The following-driver preparedness rule is covered, but the universal legal classification and any statutory crossing or load exceptions require exact current official authority before being taught as universal.

g_matrix.note: Text-supported facts are indexed; the named material source/visual gap remains open.
Exact missed-question allowance; no inferred percentage.
A motorcycle is entitled to its full lane, a truck's right-turn setup can extend left and a cyclist may need the center of a narrow lane. A flashing motorcycle indicator alone does not prove a turn.
See, leave space and wait is a teaching cue for the supported road-sharing decisions.
A right hook is a turning conflict across a cyclist's path; a sharrow marks a preferred shared-lane cycling position; a pilot vehicle warns of an unusually large load.
Dynamic and unverified service facts isolated as debt.
